findings.reason: the bullet is unreachable by the stated fix, so a worker either fails its gate or silently loosens a designed refusal, and the plan must say which.
findings.text: §14's second done-when bullet requires that "a promoted run whose review carries a blocking finding has its repair round opened within one beat", but `reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:1051` states the opposite rule as a deliberate guard: "A promoted run, or one whose live pointer has gone, is refused rather than dispatched: the reviewed run is settled, so there is no tree left to cut a repair against". No mechanism in the Deliverable changes that guard, so a node implementing §14 as written reaches a bullet it cannot satisfy without reversing a documented refusal it was never told to touch — and the section would then have to say what a repair of an already-landed tree means and against which head it is cut.

findings.reason: if the review was never requested or the sweep failed, separating the duty pass from a walk that does not exist fixes nothing, and the repair is aimed at the wrong mechanism.
findings.text: §14 names the cause as `SweepBeat.request` returning early while a session's previous sweep is in flight, and supports "can run for hours" only by quoting the class's own docstring (`reckon/crew/station.py:229`). The cited evidence — a review not dispatched for 50 minutes while a follower streamed rows, and a direct dispatch that worked at once — is equally consistent with the sweep never being requested for that session (`Station` calls `self.sweeps.request` per session at `reckon/crew/station.py:537`, gated by `_sessions_to_sweep`) or with the sweep raising before the review pass. `resumption.sweep` (`reckon/crew/resumption.py:1848`) contains no walk of registered worktrees at all; its body lists live pointers, builds resume plans and dispatches. Nothing in the record shows a sweep in flight for the 50 minutes, so the section aims at a mechanism its evidence does not select.

findings.reason: one gate proves neither deliverable, and the obligation half needs the station to publish a sweep start time that no section currently promises to record.
findings.text: §14 states two deliverables under one node: move review composition and repair dispatch off the sweep's slow path (`reckon/crew/station.py`), and make the obligation state the sweep's in-flight age instead of "within about 120 s" (`reckon/crew/obligations.py:690`, whose `_reflex_review_window_seconds` reads `DEFAULT_SWEEP_SECONDS` with no access to any sweep state). They are separate files, separate mechanisms and separate failure modes, and one verdict cannot close both.

findings.reason: the measure has no control and no named input, so it can pass on a hardcoded string and no reader could tell.
findings.text: §14's third bullet measures that the obligation "names the sweep's age rather than 'within about 120 s'", but no negative control is declared for it (the control at :462 covers only the review-not-dispatched bullet), and the plan never says which record carries a sweep's start time, so the test cannot be written without inventing that surface.

findings.reason: the plan records a defect it does not repair, so the evidence reads as covered when the node will not touch it; the author should either add a bullet or drop the instance.
findings.text: §15's Why cites a third instance, "a stale handover answered 'already admitted' for a discarded review request", but neither the Deliverable nor the done-when names any behaviour that would fix it: the three bullets cover the blocking-finding row, the advice hold, and the admission-held row's own run id, and none of them touches a handover answering for a discarded request.

findings.reason: the bullet is a cheap guard that cannot make the node's work wrong, and the first bullet's control already carries the section's falsification.
findings.text: §15's third bullet ("a row for an admission-held run names only its own run id in its command") carries no base control, and if that behaviour is already correct at base the case is a regression guard rather than a repair — which is fine, but then it proves nothing about the defect the section exists for and the section should say so.
